title: A morphism of sheaves of sets on a site is an epimorphism iff it is locally surjective
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site and $\Sh(\mathcal C)$ its category of sheaves of sets [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], and let $\varphi:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ be a morphism of $\Sh(\mathcal C)$. Then $\varphi$ is an epimorphism of $\Sh(\mathcal C)$ (for every sheaf of sets $\mathcal H$ and morphisms $a,b:\mathcal G\to\mathcal H$ with $a\circ\varphi=b\circ\varphi$ one has $a=b$) if and only if $\varphi$ is surjective in the sense of sheaves: for every object $U$ of $\mathcal C$ and every $s\in\mathcal G(U)$ there is a covering $\{U_i\to U\}_{i\in I}$ of $\mathcal C$ such that for every $i$ the restriction $s|_{U_i}$ lies in the image of $\varphi_{U_i}:\mathcal F(U_i)\to\mathcal G(U_i)$.
